name: Rab-shakeh
description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: The first example of the punishment of the proud: the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh with a great host against Jerusalem, taunting king Hezekiah: what confidence is this wherein thou trustest? He mocked their trust in Egypt, a bruised reed, and mocked their trust in the Lord, and even claimed, the Lord said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: The king of Assyria sends Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh with a great host to Jerusalem, and they stand by the conduit of the upper pool.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Rabshakeh, the ambassador of the Assyrian army, spoke for the king to convince Judah to yield. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah asked him to speak in the Syrian language, not in the Jews' language in the ears of the people on the wall. History note from class: the Assyrians and the Syrians were two distinct peoples whose languages intermingled; the Syrians are the children of Aram, Shemites, so Aramaic is Syrian, and through the migrations Aramaic slowly began to replace the paleo Hebrew we spoke.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall will not understand, but he refuses.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and tell him the words of Rabshakeh.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: It may be the Lord thy God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to reproach the living God. God heard him disrespecting the living God. Isaiah answered: be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard; behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: This follows chapter 18, where Rabshakeh the messenger of Sennacherib told Judah their God was no different from the gods of the nations Assyria had already destroyed.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

points: Rabshakeh returns and finds the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, having departed from Lachish.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

points: The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great army, and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool. Eliakim, Shebna the scribe, and Joah the recorder came out to meet him.

Eliakim and Shebna and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language, which they understand, and not in the Jews' language in the ears of the people on the wall. They do not want the people to hear the threats.

Rabshakeh refuses, saying his master sent him to the men on the wall, who are the ones set to eat their own dung and drink their own piss with them. He deliberately speaks to frighten the common people.

Rabshakeh stands and cries with a loud voice in the Jews' language, telling the people not to let Hezekiah deceive them, for he cannot deliver them. He works to break the people's trust in their king.
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and tell him the words of Rabshakeh. They bring the blasphemy before the king in mourning.
He asks that Isaiah pray for the remnant that is left, hoping the Most High will hear the words of Rabshakeh, who was sent to reproach the living God. Hezekiah seeks the prophet's intercession.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Rabshakeh returns and finds the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he had departed from Lachish. Word comes of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia coming out to make war.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians
